crossRefs.note: But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning…
Pilate therefore entered again into the Praetorium, called Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man perverting the nation, forbidding paying taxes to Caesar, and…
When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city, crying, “These who…
whom Jason has received. These all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus!”

parallels.note: An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

people.name: Pilate
people.line: Roman governor who presided over Jesus' trial

people.name: Tiberius
people.line: Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and death

translations.web: At this, Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t Caesar’s friend! Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar!”
translations.bsb: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”
translations.kjv: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Caesar's friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.
translations.asv: Upon this Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou release this man, thou art not Caesar's friend: every one that maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.
